title: Module quiz: Structured output and defensive parsing

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: An invoice extractor runs on a model that supports structured outputs. The reply has the right fields and types, yet the cited sentence is one the document never contained. Who catches it?

options.text: The API, because the schema lists the evidence field as a string type
options.says: Ruled out because "A schema cannot say that a number is at least 0, that a quotation occurs in the document".

options.text: Only the program, by searching the source text for that exact wording
options.says: The page says "If the string is not in the document, the model made it up or changed it", and the check "needs no model".

options.text: The grammar cache, which compares each reply with the earlier replies
options.says: Ruled out because the cache only holds a compiled grammar: "Compiled grammars are cached for 24 hours from last use".

options.text: The stop reason, which flags every invented sentence at the end of the reply
options.says: Ruled out because "The loop reads `stop_reason` before the body", and it reports why generation ended, not whether the text is true.

origin.section: A quotation must occur in the source

questions.stem: A team's code retries every failed reply up to five times. A document triggers a `refusal`. What is the right change?

options.text: Stop there and report it, rather than repeating the same request
options.says: The page says that "a refusal is a decision, not a malformed answer", so the loop reports it; the documented fallback model is a different request, not a repeat.

options.text: Add the refusal text to the next prompt, for the model to explain itself
options.says: Ruled out because "Asking again with an error list cannot fix either".

options.text: Switch to a forced tool, which accepts every document without objection
options.says: Ruled out because on some models `any` and `tool` "return a 400 error", and no tool choice overrides a refusal.

options.text: Raise the attempts to ten, so that one of the later calls gets past it
options.says: Ruled out because "The same request gets the same decision, and each call is billed."

origin.section: Stop reasons that are not retried

questions.stem: A schema has an enum of `USD`, `EUR` and `GBP`, and a reply returns `Eur`. How should the program treat it?

options.text: As a match, since the comparison should ignore capital letters in the value
options.says: The page says "Compare enum values case-insensitively, and avoid enum values that differ only in capitalization."

options.text: As a schema violation, since the characters differ from the allowed list
options.says: Ruled out because the response completes normally, "with no error and no special `stop_reason`", and the difference is only in capital letters.

options.text: As an API error, reported with a 400 status code on the request
options.says: Ruled out for the same reason, since the response is "with no error and no special `stop_reason`".

options.text: As a refusal, because the promised shape was not honoured by the model
options.says: Ruled out because "A refusal is a result to report", and it is marked by its stop reason, which this reply lacks.

questions.stem: A reply with `stop_reason` of `max_tokens` holds `{"vendor": "Acme`. Which step should the program take?

options.text: Close the braces itself and validate the value it guessed from the text
options.says: Ruled out because "guessing missing braces turns a cut-off reply into a wrong record".

options.text: Re-prompt with the error list, so that the model finishes the missing text
options.says: Ruled out because "Asking again with an error list cannot fix either: a cut-off reply needs a larger limit".

options.text: Report the status as truncated, and raise the limit before asking again
options.says: The page says "Raise `max_tokens` or continue the response", and "The reader repairs a harmless habit. It does not repair a broken value".

options.text: Treat it as a refusal and switch over to a fallback model for the retry
options.says: Ruled out because "a refusal is a decision, not a malformed answer", and a cut-off reply is a different stop reason.

origin.section: Stop reasons that are not retried
